gate: M10/1 Active; GPU decoder boundary delivered, complete hardware/app acceptance open
deliverable: Golden Decoder explicitly selects software or exact-adapter D3D11. Returned storage separates CPU planes from worker-local GPU frames; the FFmpeg frame lease pins its array slice across seeks and decoder replacement/shutdown. The existing app software path is preserved.

ownership.boundary: SoftwareDecoder is replaced by Decoder throughout current Rust callers. No obsolete alias or duplicate demux/decode state machine remains. software_image returns None for hardware storage; SoftwareImageConverter returns typed HardwareStorage rather than transferring or dereferencing GPU pointers.
ownership.adapter: Resolve the requested LUID to the current DXGI index for FFmpeg's public device creation API; each decoded frame rechecks its actual device LUID, storage, slice and visible/padded extent. No manually copied AVD3D11VADeviceContext ABI or new dependency is introduced.
ownership.pool: get_format admits only D3D11 and initializes its fixed pool through public FFmpeg frame APIs, capped at32 surfaces and the admitted padded pixel count before allocation. Eight extra work surfaces are requested. The caller must still budget all retained old pools/generations; this is not full app GPU resource admission.
ownership.lifetime: D3d11Frame retains the owned FFmpeg frame as well as its texture, so a COM AddRef alone cannot permit premature slice reuse. Hardware frames and devices are worker-local. Frame removal checks report native failure for withdrawal/reopen; an owning worker must implement recovery and explicit software fallback.
ownership.formats: NV12 and P010 storage are represented with original matrix/range/transfer metadata. Only Intel H.264 NV12 is functionally hardware-verified in this slice; P010, NVIDIA and hardware HEVC are not accepted.
